title: Heuristic Learning with Graph Neural Networks: A Unified Framework for Link Prediction

problem.claim: Link prediction is shaped by graph topology, but traditional topology-based heuristics have difficulty generalizing across diverse graphs.

gap.claim: A unified formulation accommodating both local and global heuristics had not been identified.

contributions.claim: A unified matrix formulation represents and generalizes various local and global heuristics through adjacency matrix multiplications.
HL-GNN efficiently implements the unified formulation using intra-layer propagation and inter-layer connections.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HL-GNN reaches a depth of around 20 layers with lower time complexity than GCN.
The authors report extensive experiments on the Planetoid, Amazon, and OGB datasets.

The authors report that HL-GNN outperforms existing methods by a large margin, is several orders of magnitude faster than heuristic-inspired methods, uses only a few trainable parameters, and produces highly interpretable generalized heuristics and learned weights.

narrative_sequence.summary: Link prediction depends on graph topology, while traditional heuristics face generalization challenges across diverse graphs.
Existing work lacks a unified formulation covering both local and global heuristics.
The paper introduces a unified matrix formulation and the HL-GNN architecture to implement it.
HL-GNN uses intra-layer propagation and inter-layer connections to support around 20 layers with lower time complexity than GCN.
Experiments and a case study report effectiveness, efficiency, parameter economy, and interpretability.

source_observation.claim: A matrix formulation based on adjacency matrix multiplications can accommodate both local and global heuristics.

interpretation.claim: Representing related heuristics in a shared algebraic form may support a more general learning architecture.

application.claim: When combining graph heuristics, investigate whether their propagation operations can be expressed through a common matrix formulation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this formulation generalizes beyond the reported heuristic families or datasets.

source_observation.claim: HL-GNN uses intra-layer propagation and inter-layer connections and is reported to be faster than heuristic-inspired methods with few trainable parameters.

interpretation.claim: Separating propagation within layers from connections across layers may improve computational efficiency and parameter economy.

application.claim: For deep graph models, consider architectural designs that control propagation and cross-layer communication separately.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the experimental settings, baselines, or measurements needed to assess the reported efficiency claims independently.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact matrix formulation or model architecture.
The abstract does not provide dataset splits, baseline details, quantitative results, or statistical analysis.
The abstract does not describe the case-study setup or interpretability procedure.
